$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y-7z &=-1 \\ 2x-y-11z &=-6.\end{aligned}\right.

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -7 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & -11 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -7 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & -11 & -6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -7 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -4 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=4z-5 \\ y &=-3z-4 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
